newsitem.title: USA: U.S. seeks European backing for tough line on Iran.
newsitem.headline: U.S. seeks European backing for tough line on Iran.

text.p: The United States has launched a new diplomatic mission to persuade European countries to join the U.S. hard line against Iran, the State Department announced on Monday.
Peter Tarnoff, until recently the department's number three official, is in Europe for consultations with allies on the subject, spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.

His mission is "to explore with our allies practical steps that the international community can take to change Iran's objectionable behavior, including its support for terrorism, its pursuit of weapons of mass destruction and its position to the Middle East peace process," Burns said.

Tarnoff was in The Hague on Monday where he met Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo, and then left for Bonn. He would also visit Paris and London, returning to Washington on Wednesday night, Burns said.
Tarnoff stepped down last Friday after four years as undersecretary of state for political affairs and is now serving as a special adviser to Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.

Until recently, the United States and Europe have been at logggerheads over Iran, with Washington taking a strict policy of containment bolstered by tough sanctions and the Europeans pursuing what they called a "critical dialogue."

But a Berlin court finding April 10 that Iranian leaders ordered the murders of three Kurdish dissidents and their interpreter has led most European Union countries to withdraw their ambassadors from Tehran and to drop the dialogue.

Burns said the German ruling provided a "window of opportunity" and that one of Tarnoff's aims was to try to influence European thinking before EU foreign ministers discuss Iran during a meeting in Luxembourg April 29.

Burns said Washington wanted to "fashion mutual joint policies with the Europeans that will gather the strategic objective that I think we do share with the European Union. And that is, can we modify Iran's behavior?"

Neither he nor Albright gave any indication that the United States would consider offering Iran a dialogue under certain circumstances, an idea that some experts in Washington have suggested recently.

Albright, speaking to reporters before talks with Romanian Foreign Minister Adrian Severin, said Tarnoff would "make clear that our policy will remain as it is ... we have no intention of changing our policy."
Burns said that although Washington's "ideal scenario" would be for the Europeans to adopt the same trade sanctions against Iran as the United States has done, he doubted that was realistic.
"So if the Europeans are not willing to do that, then perhaps there's some other things that we can do with them that would at least be stronger than the Western front as it now appears," he said.
